title: Regional cities offer more accessible property ladder entry
summary:
Research from Savills has identified the most affordable UK cities for first-time buyers, with Stoke-on-Trent leading with a flat price-to-income ratio of 2.5 and average flat prices of £88,448. The analysis comes as London deposits reach approximately £130,000, prompting graduates to consider regional alternatives with stronger affordability metrics.

title: Rental market survey: five cities across England and Scotland
summary:
A survey of rental properties across five cities in England and Scotland reveals monthly rental rates ranging from £950 to £1,750, reflecting regional variations in the buy-to-let market. Properties surveyed include developments in Milton Keynes, Liverpool, Norwich, Southampton and Glasgow.

title: Specialist lender approves Glasgow flat above pub
summary:
A specialist mortgage lender has completed a buy-to-let transaction for a Glasgow flat situated above commercial premises, after the application was initially declined under standard lending criteria. The one-bedroom property generates a yield of 7.9%.

title: Banks expand 100% mortgage options for first-time buyers
summary:
Several major UK lenders have introduced mortgage products requiring minimal or no deposits, marking a shift in lending practices as banks seek to support first-time buyers struggling with affordability. Metro Bank recently launched a 100% loan-to-value mortgage, joining institutions including Lloyds, Santander and building societies offering low-deposit options.

title: Land value tax could take five years to implement, says BoE
summary:
Sir John Gieve, former Deputy Governor of the Bank of England, has outlined the case for introducing a land value tax to replace existing property levies, warning that implementation could require three to five years of preparation.

title: Estate agency staff arrested amid fraud investigation
summary:
A 58-year-old man has been arrested following a police investigation into alleged fraud and money laundering at PS&B Estate Management Limited. The South of England estate agency reportedly held approximately £7 million in client funds and managed 400 blocks.

The post Estate agency staff arrested amid fraud investigation appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Councils collect only 25% of fines issued to landlords
summary:
Local authorities in England are collecting just a quarter of fines issued to landlords for housing offences, despite a 7% increase in property inspections. Of almost £30 million in fines issued between 2023/24 and 2024/25, only £7.5 million has been collected.

title: Conveyancing regulator defends actions after criticism
summary:
The Council for Licensed Conveyancers has defended its regulatory approach after criticism from the Legal Services Consumer Panel. The regulator emphasised that issues highlighted in a BBC Panorama investigation concerned unregulated estate agents rather than conveyancers.

The post Conveyancing regulator defends actions after criticism appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Half of UK property listings fail to reach completion
summary:
Only 50% of homes that leave estate agents' books in the UK are progressing to exchange and completion, according to market data for week 27 of 2026. The figures reveal persistent overvaluation issues, with a 14.4% gap between average listing prices and properties going under offer.

The post Half of UK property listings fail to reach completion appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Former BBC presenter moves into estate agency videos
summary:
Former BBC Look North presenter Christa Ackroyd has begun producing property video content for a Yorkshire estate agency, more than a decade after leaving broadcasting. Ackroyd, 69, is creating social media property tours for Hunters in Otley, West Yorkshire, on a freelance basis.
